Container.Name: WebSSH
Container.Overview:
WebSSH is a self-hosted, multi-user SSH and SFTP client in the browser: terminals with optional persistent tmux sessions, a file workspace, saved hosts, jump hosts and SOCKS5 routes, encrypted keys, host-key verification, commands, backup and restore.
Security: WebSSH is an SSH gateway. Anyone who can sign in can reach the SSH targets its network allows. This template uses the homelab profile for a trusted LAN. Do not publish it to the internet; for remote access use a VPN, or a reverse proxy with HTTPS and the production profile described in the production deployment guide: https://github.com/bifrost0x/webssh/blob/main/docs/wiki/Production-Deployment.md
First start: the first account created in the browser becomes the administrator. Open the WebUI and create it right after installation, before anyone else can reach the instance. The form asks for the setup token that WebSSH prints in the container log.
The container runs as nobody:users (99:100) without Linux capabilities, never as root. Unraid creates the appdata folders for that user on installation. Other containers running as 99:100 with access to the appdata share can read WebSSH's data; the install guide explains how to isolate it. The template sets no secret; WebSSH generates its application secret on first start and keeps it in the data folder.
Container.Requires: Keep the appdata folders private. Their contents include the application secret and encrypted SSH keys.
Container.ExtraSearchTerms: ssh sftp terminal web browser gateway tmux

Config.Name: WebUI port
Config.Description: HTTP port of the web interface. Keep it on your LAN.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: Database, generated application secret, encrypted keys and user files. Back it up and keep it private.

Config.Name: Recovery
Config.Description: Durable backup and restore staging, including rollback copies. Keep it outside the data folder.

Config.Name: Deployment profile
Config.Description: homelab keeps HTTP and private-network compatibility for a trusted LAN. Use production only behind HTTPS as documented.

Config.Name: Allowed origins
Config.Description: Origins allowed to open WebSSH. '*' accepts any address you use on the LAN; set exact origins such as http://tower:5000 to restrict it.

Config.Name: Allow origin wildcard
Config.Description: Permits '*' in Allowed origins for the homelab profile. Set false when you list exact origins.

Config.Name: Trusted proxies
Config.Description: Number of reverse proxies in front of WebSSH. 0 for direct LAN access.

Config.Name: Secure cookies
Config.Description: Set true when WebSSH is only reached over HTTPS.

Config.Name: tmux session prefix
Config.Description: Name prefix for persistent tmux sessions on remote hosts.

Config.Name: TOTP available
Config.Description: Deployment-level switch for authenticator-app MFA. Administrators still decide in the interface whether users can enroll.

Config.Name: OIDC MFA amr values
Config.Description: Only for OpenID Connect: signed amr values your provider documents as MFA. Leave empty otherwise.

Config.Name: OIDC MFA acr values
Config.Description: Only for OpenID Connect: signed acr values your provider documents as MFA. Leave empty otherwise.

Config.Name: OIDC phishing-resistant amr values
Config.Description: Only for OpenID Connect: signed amr values for phishing-resistant MFA. Leave empty otherwise.

Config.Name: OIDC phishing-resistant acr values
Config.Description: Only for OpenID Connect: signed acr values for phishing-resistant MFA. Leave empty otherwise.

Config.Name: OIDC step-up acr values
Config.Description: Only for OpenID Connect: acr values requested for step-up authentication. Leave empty otherwise.

Config.Name: Step-up maximum age
Config.Description: Seconds a step-up authentication stays valid for sensitive administrator actions.

Config.Name: Backup staging directory
Config.Description: Container path for backup and restore staging. Keep the default so it uses the Recovery folder.

Config.Name: Durable recovery
Config.Description: Confirms that the Recovery folder is persistent storage, which online restore requires.
